title: Closed issue status is not subcase coverage or proof of novelty
applies_when: A source-audit lead resembles a closed issue, a merged fix to a sibling method, or a multi-case report whose title mentions only one API.
lesson: Read the issue body and linked patch before deciding whether a finding is new or fixed. Separate three questions: is the behavior reproducible now, was this exact case already reported, and did the accepted patch address it? AnyIO #1081 names receive(max_bytes) in its title but also reports negative receive_exactly(nbytes) in its body. Merged #1191 adds max_bytes validation to receive implementations; the pinned buffered receive_exactly implementation still takes a negative slice. This supports returning to the existing report and clarifying the remaining contract, not a competing fresh-discovery PR. Record scoped owner advice with a reopening condition rather than suppressing the whole file or changing raw model results.
avoid_when: A closed issue can contain unresolved or distinct actionable bugs; neither its status nor a same-file match justifies rejecting a new lead. A current native failure does not prove novelty, intended behavior or maintainer acceptance. Do not copy a sibling API's positive-size constraint: zero-length exact reads can deliberately differ from bounded receive. This is one source/history counterexample, not a measured improvement in Scout conversion or a universal negative-length rule.

evidence.note: The closed report explicitly includes negative and zero receive_exactly cases and reproducer tests, beyond the receive(max_bytes) API named in its title. It establishes prior reporting, not the final contract for every case.
The merged follow-on describes validation of max_bytes in ByteReceiveStream.receive implementations. Its closure of #1081 alone does not establish receive_exactly coverage.

Pinned source still uses buffer[:nbytes] when remaining <= 0, with no negative-nbytes guard. This is scoped current-source evidence, not proof that the behavior is supported, novel or accepted for repair.
